question_text: Consider the statement: 'To improve student outcomes, the school will extend daily study hours from 6 to 8 hours.' Two assumptions follow. explanation: Both Assumptions I and II are implicit — the decision to extend hours only makes sense if (I) more hours are believed to improve outcomes and (II) the current duration is seen as inadequate; rejecting either would make the school's action irrational. Assumption I is the causal premise: without believing hours drive outcomes, extending them has no rationale. Assumption II is the diagnostic premise: if 6 hours were sufficient, there would be no problem requiring a solution. Options A and C each accept only one assumption, but both are needed to justify the school's decision.
option_text: Only Assumption I is implicit.
